newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Little in sight to spoil party for OLOs - dealers.
newsitem.headline: Little in sight to spoil party for OLOs - dealers.

text.p: Belgian government bonds (OLOs) and bond futures pared their earlier gains after Tuesday's exchange auction, but dealers foresaw no marked interruption to the current bull run inspired by hopes of steady interest rates.

The market might see some yield spread widening in the 10- year area versus Bunds to eight to 10 basis points from five bps at 1630 GMT, but that would reflect the "usual" jockeying for positions before next week's outright OLO auction, they said.
Volume could pick up in the second half of the week, which will see U.S. CPI, German M3, IFO data on the German economy and a Bundesbank council meeting.

One trader said the focus would be on the CPI figures, "but they will have to be very negative to have an impact...I see little that could disturb the party here." are counting on the Bundesbank not changing German interest rates as long as the economy remains weak DE-ECI.
"Overall, unless the U.S. CPI or the German Bundesbank come up with surprises, the bullish trend should remain intact," said another.
An expected test of the 5.50 percent yield level had come earlier than expected, he added.

"Belgian end-investors are still buyers," said a trader. It was unclear when players would run out of appetite. "I thought we reached overbought levels long ago, but as long as there is domestic demand..." Volumes were low, he noted.

The benchmark 10-year yield BE286= slipped to 5.50 percent in the course of the day from 5.52 last week and 5.70 the week before, but did not hold that level. It was at 5.54 percent at 1650 GMT. "Its performance is still impressive," said another.
The benchmark, also known as OLO 26, came under some selling pressure after today's exchange auction at which the issue was on offer together with a number of others.

Of the benchmark paper, 49.71 billion francs worth was sold at the auction. "It will be interesting to see over the next few days where the paper went...if it is in portfolios fine, if it is in trading positions it will come out," a trader said.

Fundamentally-oriented players said Belgium's strong current account surplus, subdued inflation, a recovering economy and good EMU prospects meant OLOs should not be sold. Another said OLOs needed a major correction to become a 'buy'. This view would rob OLOs of much upward potential, definitely before Monday's OLO auction, but also with a view to nervousness about the course of U.S. rates. -- Nieck Ammerlaan, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6816, Fax +32 2 230 7710
